solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Scrounge a large one (6)

blocks.note: to bum a cigarette is to scrounge one
per = a, as in 'ten pounds a head'

annotation.surface: Someone cadging a big helping of something.
annotation.walkthrough: The first 'a' is worth PER, while the article in 'a large one' belongs to the definition, so the clue splits after 'Scrounge a'.
annotation.definitionFit: Bumper is used as a noun for anything unusually big of its kind, a sense most familiar from bumper crop or bumper issue.

entries.clue: Postwar child peeled tropical fruit that’s seen in Australia (9)

indicatorNotes.peeled: peeling fruit strips away its skin, so the outside letters of the fruit's name come off

blocks.note: a baby boomer, born in the postwar birth surge
MANGO without its first and last letters

annotation.surface: A baby boomer eating a peeled mango somewhere in Australia.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is only a loose description, but the boomerang is the object most associated with Australia; the mango fits the tropical north, which helps the disguise.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by association: the Aboriginal throwing stick is an emblem of Australia, so it is the thing you would expect to see there.

entries.clue: Police on radio evacuated transit network (5)

indicatorNotes.evacuated: an evacuated building has had everyone inside cleared out, so the word keeps only its shell

blocks.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police
RADIO with its middle letters removed

annotation.surface: Police radioing about the evacuation of an underground railway.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On' is a placing word here: in a down clue the police piece sits on top of the radio piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Metro is the general word for an underground city railway, taken from the Paris Métro.

entries.clue: Sudden insight: northbound Tube convenient when dropping daughter (8)

indicatorNotes.northbound: in a down clue north is up the grid, so a northbound word is read from the bottom
indicatorNotes.dropping: to drop something is to let it fall away, so the daughter's letter falls out of the word

annotation.surface: A commuter's flash of inspiration: the northbound Underground is handy for the school drop-off.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital T on 'Tube' makes you think of the London Underground, but it is just a pipe. Dropping a daughter off at school is part of the surface's school run.
annotation.definitionFit: An epiphany is a moment of sudden revelation, a sense extended from the Christian feast of Christ being revealed to the Magi.

entries.clue: Controlling figure succeeded; very English — The Greatest! (8)

blocks.note: Muhammad Ali called himself The Greatest

annotation.surface: A sports headline hailing a triumphant English champion as the greatest.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface's triumph is a red herring; 'succeeded' is the one-letter abbreviation. Svengali is the hypnotist in George du Maurier's novel Trilby.
annotation.definitionFit: A fictional name turned common noun: after du Maurier's mesmerist, a svengali is anyone who manipulates and dominates another.

entries.clue: Roughly 4 hour wait finally for buck (8,5)

indicatorNotes.Roughly: something handled roughly is knocked about, so the letters are knocked into a new order
indicatorNotes.finally: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of the next word is used

blocks.note: the answer to 4 across, used as fodder

annotation.surface: A four-hour wait for a dollar, or for a male deer.
annotation.walkthrough: '4' is a cross-reference to 4 across, not the number, so the fodder is that answer. 'Buck' suggests a dollar or a stag; here it is gym equipment.
annotation.definitionFit: A gymnastics sense: a buck is a short padded block on legs that gymnasts vault over, a smaller version of the full-length horse.

entries.clue: Visiting Namibia on vacation, ordered blue Crab for one (6)

indicatorNotes.Visiting: a visitor stays inside someone else's place, so the rearranged letters go inside the other piece
indicatorNotes.on vacation: a place on vacation has been vacated, emptied of its contents, so only the outside letters remain
indicatorNotes.ordered: to order things is to arrange them, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram of BLUE, placed inside NA

annotation.surface: A blue crab turning up in Namibia on holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital C is the tell: this is the Crab Nebula in Taurus, not a crustacean.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the Crab Nebula, remnant of a supernova, is one instance of a cloud of gas and dust in space.

entries.clue: Art Basel reeling after mag exposed material used in column (9)

indicatorNotes.reeling: reeling means staggering about, so the letters stagger into a new order
indicatorNotes.after: in a down clue, coming after means sitting below the earlier piece
indicatorNotes.exposed: exposed means stripped of covering, so the word loses its outer letters

blocks.note: MAG with its outer letters removed

annotation.surface: A magazine exposé leaves the Art Basel fair reeling after a column on it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Column' pretends to be a magazine column, but it is a stone pillar. Art Basel is an international art fair held in Switzerland.
annotation.definitionFit: Alabaster, a soft white stone easy to carve, has long been worked into pillars, so the definition describes a use rather than giving a synonym.

entries.clue: Peace-loving inspiration finds herself in dire need (5)

indicatorNotes.in: in marks the answer as lying inside the words that follow, running across the gap

blocks.note: the letters run across the word break, dropping the outer D and D

annotation.surface: A pacifist muse discovering she is in desperate straits.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Herself' confirms a female answer, hidden in d-IRE NE-ed. Irene (Eirene) is the Greek goddess of peace.
annotation.definitionFit: A mythological sense: Eirene was the goddess who embodied peace, and her name is simply the Greek word for it.

entries.clue: Large sighs heard following umpire’s decision (7)

indicatorNotes.heard: what is heard is the sound, so the word is replaced by one that sounds the same
indicatorNotes.following: following means coming after, so this piece goes second

blocks.note: a cricket umpire gives a batsman out

annotation.surface: A crowd sighing heavily after an umpire gives a batsman out.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition leads and reads as an adjective on 'sighs', which hides it well.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used mostly of clothing: outsize garments are extra-large ones.

entries.clue: Hemlines and belt tailored to capture masculine finishing touch (13)

indicatorNotes.tailored: tailoring cuts and reshapes cloth, so the letters are cut and reshaped
indicatorNotes.to capture: to capture is to take inside, so the letter goes within the others

blocks.note: m = masculine, captured inside the anagram

annotation.surface: A dressmaker adjusting hemlines and a belt as a final flourish.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue stays in the sewing room, so the definition blends in; 'and' is only surface glue between the two fodder words.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: an embellishment is a decorative addition, the kind of detail added last to finish a piece off.

entries.clue: One leaving Italian region, say, reflected resentment (7)

indicatorNotes.leaving: something leaving goes away, so that letter departs from the region's name
indicatorNotes.reflected: a reflection in a mirror reads backwards, so the letters reverse

annotation.surface: An emigrant leaving Umbria looks back with bitterness.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Say' is the usual signal for an example, EG, which then reverses.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, usually met in the phrase to take umbrage, meaning to take offence.

entries.clue: Return to manage hotel for a period (5)

indicatorNotes.Return: to return is to go back the way you came, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: H = hotel in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Coming back to run a hotel for a while.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Return to manage' reads as a comeback to management, but 'to manage' is the verb COPE, reversed.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with the flavour of a distinctive era, as in a geological epoch.

entries.clue: A vote introduced by British PM for disused weapon (6-3)

indicatorNotes.introduced by: to be introduced by someone is to be brought in by them, so the vote goes inside the PM's name

blocks.note: taken as written, goes inside ATTLEE
a cross on the ballot paper

annotation.surface: A British prime minister bringing in a vote on an old weapon.
annotation.walkthrough: 'PM' could be any premier or the afternoon; Attlee, Labour prime minister after the Second World War, is the one whose name fits. The word lives on for a formidable woman.
annotation.definitionFit: A historical sense: the broad-bladed war axe went out of military use centuries ago, so it is fairly called disused.

entries.clue: A style of dress worn by geek back to front, hence the rush? (10)

indicatorNotes.worn by: clothes worn by someone sit alongside them, so the dress piece is put next to the geek piece
indicatorNotes.back to front: back to front means reversed, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: an A-line dress flares from the shoulders or waist

annotation.surface: A geek wearing a dress back to front, and the thrill that follows.
annotation.walkthrough: 'A style of dress' reads as one phrase, but the A is split off and an A-line dress is still needed after the reversed geek.
annotation.definitionFit: A metonym: the thrill of excitement is called an adrenaline rush after the hormone behind it, so the rush can stand for the hormone.

entries.clue: File blunder in Times article on Bush? (9)

indicatorNotes.in: in places one piece inside another, so the blunder goes inside the multiplication word

blocks.note: a rasp is a coarse file
as in 3 by 4 = 3 times 4; ERR goes inside

annotation.surface: A newspaper story on President Bush's gaffe, filed in The Times.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital T makes 'Times' a newspaper, but it means multiplied by. The definition is a pun: the fruit grows on a bush, and a raspberry is also the rude noise one might blow at Bush.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the berry is an item that hangs on a bush, and the question mark admits the double reading.

entries.clue: Stop big name in NYC sport making a comeback (4)

indicatorNotes.making a comeback: a comeback is a return, so the name comes back the other way

blocks.note: the Mets, New York's baseball team

annotation.surface: A plea to halt a New York sports star's return.
annotation.walkthrough: The New York Mets are a Major League Baseball team, a big name in the city's sport.
annotation.definitionFit: A verb synonym, used of flows: to stem the tide or stem the bleeding is to stop it.

entries.clue: Curative network set up to support wealthy Florentines (9)

indicatorNotes.set up: in a down clue, set up means raised, so the word is read upwards
indicatorNotes.to support: a support holds something up from beneath, so in a down clue this piece goes below

annotation.surface: A healing network established with Florentine money.
annotation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads in the opposite order from the surface: the family comes first in the answer even though the network is named first in the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain adjective synonym: medicinal and curative both describe something with healing power.

entries.clue: Photo of biscuits fresh from the oven? (8)

annotation.surface: A picture of just-baked cookies.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark covers the image of snaps that are hot. Biscuits is the British word for cookies.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a snapshot is an informal, quickly taken photograph.

entries.clue: My waterproof shoe? A pound wasted (4)

indicatorNotes.wasted: something wasted is thrown away, so those letters are discarded

blocks.note: GALOSH loses A and L (pound, from libra)

annotation.surface: Someone lamenting a pound spent on a rubber overshoe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'My' reads as a possessive, but it is the exclamation, as in 'My, how you've grown!'
annotation.definitionFit: Two interjections of mild surprise that can replace each other: 'My!' and 'Gosh!'.

entries.clue: With which to direct cast delivering line? (7,3)

annotation.definition: With which to direct cast delivering line?

blocks.note: the surface wants a director guiding actors; an angler's cast is the throw, and the rod aims it
not an actor delivering a line of dialogue, but the fishing line being sent out over the water

annotation.surface: A theatre director guiding the cast through their lines.
annotation.walkthrough: Cast, delivering and line all belong to the stage, but an angler casts the line and uses the rod to direct it.
annotation.definitionFit: Read as angling, the whole clue describes the rod: the tool that directs a cast as it sends out the line.

entries.clue: Drive empty Bugatti into swimming pool (6)

indicatorNotes.empty: an empty car has nothing inside, so the word keeps only its outside letters
indicatorNotes.into: driving into something puts you inside it, so this piece goes inside the pool

blocks.note: a lido is a public open-air pool

annotation.surface: Someone driving an empty Bugatti into a swimming pool.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drive' seems to start the car story but is the noun: sex drive.
annotation.definitionFit: A psychological sense: libido is the sex drive, so drive in that sense is a fair synonym.

entries.clue: US newspaper owner, drug dealer, carrying about 454 grams? (9)

indicatorNotes.carrying: a dealer carrying goods holds them on his person, so the weight goes inside
indicatorNotes.about: about can mean turned around, as in about-turn, so the letters reverse

blocks.note: 454 grams is 1 LB, written ILB and reversed

annotation.surface: An American press baron exposed as a dealer carrying a pound of drugs.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 454 grams must first become '1 lb', with the digit read as I.
annotation.definitionFit: An American usage: on a US paper the publisher is the owner or chief executive, not merely the firm that prints it.

entries.clue: Roly-poly pudding for starters topped with fruit (5)

indicatorNotes.for starters: starters come first, so only the first letter is used
indicatorNotes.topped with: in a down clue, topped with puts the named piece above

annotation.surface: A roly-poly pudding with fruit on top.
annotation.walkthrough: Jam roly-poly is a British rolled suet pudding, which makes 'Roly-poly pudding' look like one dish; here roly-poly is the definition, meaning chubby.
annotation.definitionFit: Two adjectives for a pleasantly round figure: a roly-poly child is a plump one.

entries.clue: Global outbreak has Democrat fleeing in terror (5)

indicatorNotes.fleeing: to flee is to run away, so those letters run out of the word

blocks.note: PANDEMIC loses DEM, short for Democrat

annotation.surface: A pandemic sends a Democrat running scared.
annotation.walkthrough: DEM is the usual short form of Democrat; the surface's fear is exactly the answer, which makes the definition easy to overlook.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: panic is terror that takes over and makes people act wildly.

entries.clue: Breaking news: yellow regularly ignored in material (5)

indicatorNotes.Breaking: breaking into something means forcing a way inside it, so these letters go inside the other piece
indicatorNotes.regularly ignored: ignoring at regular intervals skips every other letter

blocks.note: news as the plural of new, N N
Y, L, O: the first, third and fifth letters of YELLOW

annotation.surface: A news bulletin that skips the yellow in a fabric report.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Breaking news' reads as a TV banner, but 'Breaking' tells the yellow letters to break into the news.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: nylon is one kind of material, the synthetic fibre used for stockings and rope.

entries.clue: Elevate university commendation (7)

annotation.surface: A university honour that lifts someone up.
annotation.walkthrough: A plain charade: the definition comes first and the pieces follow in order.
annotation.definitionFit: A literary verb synonym: upraise is an old-fashioned way of saying raise up.

entries.clue: Troop formation has no shelter retreating, Switzerland admitted (7)

indicatorNotes.retreating: troops retreating go backwards, so the letters run backwards
indicatorNotes.admitted: someone admitted is let inside, so the country code goes into the reversed letters

annotation.surface: Troops caught without cover pulling back and taking refuge in Switzerland.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Has no shelter' reads as a plight, but NO and LEE are both used as letters, and CH goes after the first E.
annotation.definitionFit: A military sense: an echelon is a stepped formation in which each unit is set back diagonally from the one ahead.

entries.clue: City of Olympus almost ruined prominent couple from Thebes (8)

indicatorNotes.almost: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
indicatorNotes.ruined: something ruined is wrecked, so the letters are wrecked into a new order
indicatorNotes.prominent couple from: the prominent part of a word is its front, so the first two letters are taken

blocks.note: the two leading letters of THEBES

annotation.surface: Two famous Thebans lament a ruined city on Mount Olympus.
annotation.walkthrough: 'City of Olympus' looks like the definition, but the city is only 'City'. Plymouth is a port in Devon, England.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: Plymouth is a city in south-west England, famous as the Pilgrim Fathers' port.

entries.clue: Uptight, nursing temperature, oxygen off the scale (6)

indicatorNotes.nursing: nursing means holding close, like a baby in the arms, so the other letters go inside

annotation.surface: A tense patient with a fever and on oxygen, their readings off the charts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Off the scale' sounds like extreme readings, but it means music not written in any key.
annotation.definitionFit: A musical pun: atonal music abandons key, so it is literally off the scale rather than extreme.
